items.stem: Suppose we fit the linear model Y = Xβ + ε using least squares, where Y = (Y₁, …, Yₙ)ᵀ and ε = (ε₁, …, εₙ)ᵀ. Here X is an n × p non-stochastic matrix with full column rank and the εᵢ are i.i.d. with mean 0 and variance 1. For i ∈ {1, …, n}, let Ŷᵢ be the fitted value of Yᵢ and ε̂ᵢ the corresponding residual. For r, s ∈ {1, …, n}, r ≠ s, which of the following must be true?
statements: The random variables ε_r and Ŷ_s are uncorrelated
The random variables ε_s and Ŷ_s are uncorrelated
The random variables ε̂_r and Ŷ_s are uncorrelated
The random variables ε̂_s and Ŷ_s are uncorrelated
items.explanation: Fitted values and residuals are orthogonal projections of Y: Cov(ε̂, Ŷ) = (I − H) Var(Y) H = (I − H)H = 0 (C and D). The true errors are correlated with the fitted values through H (A and B fail).

A.why: Ŷ = HY with H = X(XᵀX)⁻¹Xᵀ, so Cov(ε, Ŷ) = H and Cov(ε_r, Ŷ_s) = h_sr, which is generally non-zero.

B.why: Cov(ε_s, Ŷ_s) = h_ss, the leverage, which is positive.

C.why: Cov(ε̂, Ŷ) = (I − H)H = 0 because H is idempotent; every entry is 0.

D.why: Same matrix identity: the diagonal entry of (I − H)H is 0.

items.stem: Suppose X ~ N(0, 1) and the conditional distribution of Y given X = x is N(αx, 1), for 0 < α < 1. When we regress Y on X, the coefficient of determination R² is
items.explanation: Y = αX + ε with ε ~ N(0, 1) independent of X. Var(Y) = α² + 1 and Cov(X, Y) = α. R² = ρ² = α²/(1 × (1 + α²)) = α²/(1 + α²): the explained variance α² over the total α² + 1.
